references.text: The same command to love the Lord with all your heart and all your soul, which expands on what it means to seek God with all your heart.
Jeremiah repeats the promise that they will find God when they seek him with all their heart.
The prophet Azariah confirms the principle: The Lord is with you when you are with him, and if you seek him, you will find him.
Israel turned to the Lord in their distress, sought him, and found him—a fulfillment of the promise in Deuteronomy 4:29.
Isaiah urges people to seek the Lord while he may be found, and call on him while he is near.
Blessed are those who keep his testimonies and seek him with all their heart.
The psalmist seeks God with all his heart, as a prayer not to let him wander astray.
Jesus promises that the one who seeks will find, a New Testament confirmation of this principle.
Paul speaks of how God arranged it so that people would seek him, perhaps grope for him and find him.
Without faith it is impossible to please God, for whoever comes to him must believe that he exists and rewards those who seek him.
